# Relationships

## Core connection

Needs are represented through requirements. Systems are intended to meet requirements. Their usefulness is understood through their contribution to the relevant needs and requirements. The [accepted adequacy rule](concepts/requirement.md#from-requirement-fulfillment-to-need-fulfillment) explains the connection between meeting requirements and meeting a need.

The particular environment determines whether systems work together, serve as alternatives or are arranged another way, according to its needs, requirements and use cases. Manifold does not prescribe that choice or require a universal combination scheme. A case can describe its chosen arrangement when useful. See the [scope decision](../../notes/decisions/environment-specific-system-arrangements.md).

A relevant contribution can be partial or indirect. Intended contribution is not demonstrated fulfillment, and an unknown contribution is not established absence of usefulness. Use the [accepted fulfillment meanings](../assessment/requirement-and-need-fulfillment.md) for those distinctions.

## Further relationship vocabulary

The vocabulary below remains proposed. The accepted core connection above does not require every further relationship to have a universal formal schema before Manifold can be defined.

| Relationship | Interpretation and caution |
| --- | --- |
| is a kind of | Classification among kinds; not membership in an operating whole |
| is an instance of | Particular thing classified by a kind; does not imply an event |
| is part of | Constituent membership in a specified whole and sense |
| depends on | Relies on something that may be outside the chosen boundary |
| contributes to | Has an explained expected or observed role in an outcome; neither membership nor proof of sufficiency |
| justified by / derived from | Links a requirement to a need, assumption or parent; retain rationale |
| performed by / accountable to | Distinct participation and responsibility relations with scoped authority |
| uses / produces | Activity input and output relationships |
| supports / challenges | Evidential relation to a particular claim |
| supersedes | A later decision or revision replaces an earlier one within scope; retain history |

Requirements describe desired conditions and need not be constituent operating parts. A supporting source and an execution record may both be evidence without sharing every other classification. Multiple contribution edges do not establish a causal explanation or additive fulfillment score.

[Classification](../taxonomy/classification-rules.md), [composition](../mereology/composition-and-boundaries.md), [execution](../execution/behavior-and-responsibility.md) and [assessment](../assessment/requirement-and-need-fulfillment.md) apply the vocabulary. Relation constraints and naming are EOM-01/EOM-10 in [the ledger](../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a).
